nodes.name: Sunlight and dry-season heat
nodes.desc: Strong sun and heat, up to about 40 C in the May to October dry season, drive the savanna growth and its seasonal browning.

nodes.name: Scarce, seasonal rain
nodes.desc: The islands have one of the driest climates in Indonesia, with roughly 800 to 1,000 mm of rain a year, so growth is tied to the wet season.

nodes.name: Volcanic island soils
nodes.desc: Thin soils over rugged volcanic hills support the savanna grasses and dry deciduous woodland of the islands.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil. Scrubfowl mounds also rely on rotting litter for heat.

nodes.name: Kangaroo grass
nodes.desc: A tussock grass named among the savanna grasses of the park, and a main food of its grazers.

nodes.name: Black speargrass
nodes.desc: Another tall savanna grass listed for the park, growing alongside kangaroo grass on the dry hillsides.

nodes.name: Lontar palm
nodes.desc: The palm that gives the dry savanna its scattered skyline. Its fallen fruit feed ground-dwelling animals.

nodes.name: Tamarind
nodes.desc: A tree of the dry deciduous forest on the islands, dropping pods and leaf litter beneath it.

nodes.name: Indian jujube
nodes.desc: A thorny dry-country fruit tree recorded in the area, offering fruit to birds and mammals.

nodes.name: Timor deer (Javan rusa)
nodes.desc: Grazes grass, leaves and fallen fruit. It is the main prey of the Komodo dragon on the park islands.

nodes.name: Feral water buffalo
nodes.desc: A grazer living wild on Komodo and Rinca. Adult dragons also take buffalo.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots for plant matter and small animals. A regular food of adult Komodo dragons.

nodes.name: Crab-eating macaque
nodes.desc: A fruit-eating monkey recorded often on the islands, an omnivore that forages for fruit.

nodes.name: Orange-footed scrubfowl
nodes.desc: A megapode that eats seeds, fallen fruit and invertebrates, incubating eggs in mounds of rotting leaf litter.

nodes.name: Black rat
nodes.desc: An introduced rodent that eats seeds and fruit, and is prey for cats and civets.

nodes.name: Large-billed crow
nodes.desc: An omnivorous scavenger of carcasses and small animals, among the most recorded birds of the area.

nodes.name: Asian palm civet
nodes.desc: An omnivorous nocturnal civet that eats fruit as well as small animals such as rats.

nodes.name: Feral cat
nodes.desc: A feral predator of rats and other small animals on the islands.

nodes.name: Komodo dragon
nodes.desc: The largest lizard. Adults ambush deer, pigs and buffalo and also eat carrion; young eat insects, birds, eggs and small reptiles.
